maya: Heads-up — onboarding solace13b (int4) on canary fleet and we keep seeing soft OOMs under bursty traffic. Happens when a few concurrent requests generate long tails.
maya: Batch defaults are batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=512, prefetch enabled. Logs show allocation failure during KV cache growth: 
maya: ```
[oom] gpu_alloc failed: tried to alloc 128MB, free 64MB, fragmentation_highwater=0.78
kv_cache_grow: from 8MB to 20MB
```
maya: Anyone seen this pattern (frag + small per-request spikes) and quick mitigations? :thinking_face:

jordan: can you paste the model profile / config you used for the canary?

maya: sure, snippet below: 
maya: ```json
{"model": "solace13b-int4", "batching": {"enabled": true, "batch_size": 4, "max_latency_ms": 40}, "generation": {"max_new_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0.7}, "prefetch": true}
```

maya: repro script: 20 concurrent users sending variable-length prompts (avg 200 tokens), spikes push many to >400 tokens.

ashley: first try: lower defaults to reduce transient memory pressure — set `max_new_tokens` -> 128 for canary, and `batch_size` -> 1 or 2 for the model profile. That avoids big simultaneous KV growth.
ashley: also enable `kv_prune_threshold=0.6` (short-term) so cache trims earlier during bursts. Tradeoff: slightly higher token recompute for long contexts.

rik: +1. Another quick knob: disable prefetch for this model (`prefetch=false`) — prefetch improves latency for steady state but increases fragmentation when many warmups happen concurrently.
rik: if we need better tail latency, consider adaptive batching (cwnd) rather than fixed batch_size=4.

luis: diagnostics to help triage: turn on `--mem-trace=per-request` on a single canary pod and run the repro. Capture KV cache sizes and peak GPU alloc per request. Also run `nvidia-smi dmon` and `tegrastats` equivalent to correlate.

maya: ran single-pod mem-trace with 50-request burst. Findings: peak per-request + kv growth spikes align. Attached minimal CSV: peak_alloc_mb: [320, 410, 380, 540, 360] (one hit at 540MB triggered OOM).

ashley: ok that aligns with fragmentation not a leak. Short-term fix: update model profile in catalog to: `{"batch_size": 1, "max_new_tokens": 128, "prefetch": false, "kv_prune_threshold": 0.6}` and push a canary of 10% traffic. Also set an automatic fallback policy to a smaller variant (solace13b-lite) on OOM.

rik: we should also add a runtime guard: if free_gpu_mem < 200MB then reject new generation with 503 (circuit) instead of trying and failing — improves SLOs.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: solace13b-int4 profile update -> 10% traffic. Watch OOM alerts on `eng-ml/model-oom`.

luis: plan for root cause: schedule a 1hr session to test with quantized kernels disabled (int4 kernel path sometimes fragments on our CUDA version) vs intel packs. Might be kernel allocator fragmentation.

maya: thanks all — I'll roll the temporary profile change now, keep logs up for 1hr and report back. :raised_hands:

ashley: thanks — if 10% passes for 1hr, promote to 50% and prepare rollback playbook (restore old profile + scale up smaller variant).

maya: update: after 40m canary, no new OOMs at 10%. One latency tail but acceptable. Will promote to 50% in 20m.

rik: nice. follow-up: add an integration test for long-tail churn to CI so future models get the same stress before canary.

maya: noted — creating a short runbook and will attach to the model onboarding PR.
